title: Regular-sequence kernels are independent of an essentially finite type regular local presentation
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a commutative local $k$-algebra essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Let $P$ and $Q$ be commutative regular local $k$-algebras [def-weil-regular-scheme], both essentially of finite type over $k$, and let $u:P\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $v:Q\twoheadrightarrow A$ be surjective local $k$-algebra homomorphisms (a local homomorphism sends the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal). Then $\ker u$ is generated by a finite $P$-regular sequence contained in the maximal ideal of $P$ if and only if $\ker v$ is generated by a finite $Q$-regular sequence contained in the maximal ideal of $Q$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Empty sequences are allowed. No completeness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 00SF (lemma-lci-local), equivalence of conditions (1) and (2), with the local complete-intersection condition expanded by Tag 00SD (definition-lci-local-ring). Over the field k, essentially finite type and essentially finite presentation agree.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-compatible-polynomial-fraction-presentations] to the surjective $k$-algebra maps $u,v$, whose sources are essentially of finite type. Obtain $D=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s]$ and maps $f:D\to P$, $g:D\to Q$ with $u f=v g=:h$. For each $p\in P$ it gives $a,t$ in the $x$-polynomial subalgebra with $f(t)$ a unit and $p f(t)=f(a)$; for each $q\in Q$ it gives $c,z$ in the $y$-polynomial subalgebra with $g(z)$ a unit and $q g(z)=g(c)$. Viewed in $D$, these are exactly the two fraction hypotheses of step 2.

Apply [lem-trf-common-localization-surjective-diagram] to the underlying ring maps $f,g,u,v$. The polynomial fraction witnesses from step 1 are also witnesses in $D$; $P,Q,A$ are local rings and $u,v$ are local surjections by hypothesis. Thus $\mathfrak n=h^{-1}(\mathfrak m_A)$ is prime and $T=D_{\mathfrak n}$ has surjective local ring maps $\alpha:T\to P$, $\beta:T\to Q$, $\gamma:T\to A$, with $u\alpha=\gamma=v\beta$. These are equalities of maps on the same ring $T$, as needed for comparing their kernels.

source.place: Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization), common prime-local extension and fraction surjectivity

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring] to the $r+s$ variables of $D$ (renumbered as one finite list) and the prime $\mathfrak n$ of step 2. Thus $T=D_{\mathfrak n}$ is regular local. Apply [lem-trf-regular-local-surjection-kernel-comparison] to $T\xrightarrow{\alpha}P\xrightarrow{u}A$: both maps are surjective local and $T,P$ are regular local. Since $u\alpha=\gamma$, their composite kernel is exactly $\ker\gamma$. Hence its finite regular-sequence property in $\mathfrak m_T$ is equivalent to that of $\ker u$ in $\mathfrak m_P$.

Apply [lem-trf-regular-local-surjection-kernel-comparison] to $T\xrightarrow{\beta}Q\xrightarrow{v}A$. The maps are surjective local ring homomorphisms by step 2, and $T,Q$ are regular local by step 3 and the original hypothesis. The equality $v\beta=\gamma$ identifies this composite kernel with the same ideal $\ker\gamma\subseteq T$ used in step 3. Thus the regular-sequence properties of $\ker u$ and $\ker v$ are equivalent through that one ideal. Both comparisons allow empty sequences and require no completeness.
